steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
GitHub comes up in phone jobs (Phone 2–3) and building apps (App 2–3). Today you'll just look around a real repository and learn the 7 words you need.

  • Time: 10 minutes
  • You need: a web browser (a phone is fine). No sign-up needed.
  • The repository: Earlln's workout app EarllnCore ↗
Links open in a new tab. Switch between GitHub and this page as you go.

steps.title: This is what GitHub is
steps.html:
GitHub is a service that keeps files on the internet. It differs from plain storage in three ways.

  1. It keeps a history — who changed what, and when.
  2. You can go back — even if something breaks.
  3. Changes get reviewed — you look at them and decide whether to 'merge'.

That's why Claude uses GitHub when working in the cloud: you can see and approve what it changed.

steps.title: Look around a repository
steps.html:
Open the EarllnCore repository ↗.

RepositoryOne folder inside GitHub. Make one per thing: one app, one set of notes
Public · PrivateThe label next to the name. Public: anyone can see it. Private: only you
READMEThe repository's introduction. It shows below the file list
steps.alt: The EarllnCore front page: Public label, main branch, commit count, files, README

check.q: Is there a Public label next to the name, and a README introduction below?

steps.title: If the screen looks different
steps.html:
• On a phone the README is further down. Scroll down.
  • If the GitHub app opens, that works too.

steps.title: Commit = a saved record
steps.html:
Tap 🕘 Commits (the clock icon) above the file list.

Each line is a commit. Like 'saving' in a game, each save of changes adds one line, with one sentence on what changed.

The 7 characters beside it (e.g. 0723207) are that record's tag. You can go back to that moment any time.
steps.alt: A list of commits: one sentence on what changed, and a tag

check.q: Can you see a line like "Rename app to EarllnCore…" in the commit list?

steps.title: If you can't find Commits
steps.html:
• On a phone it's above the file list or in the ⋯ menu.
  • Or add /commits to the end of the repository address.

steps.title: Branch = a side copy
steps.html:
The ⑂ main at the top left of the repository is a branch.

mainThe original. The app's "official version"
Other branchesA side copy for trying changes without touching the original. Claude always saves to a new branch when working in the cloud

If you like what changed on the new branch, you merge it into the original (main) with a PR, coming up next.

steps.title: PR (pull request) and merge
steps.html:
Open EarllnCore's closed PRs ↗, tap one, and look at the Files changed tab.

PRA review request: "May I merge this branch into the original?"
Files changedThe changed lines. Red is removed, green is added (just like the permission cards in Desktop 2)
MergeReview it and combine it into the original. A purple Merged means it's already in
steps.alt: Red and green lines in a PR's Files changed, with a Merged label

check.q: Can you see red and green lines in Files changed?

steps.title: If the PR list is empty
steps.html:
• Tap Closed above the list. Merged PRs live there.
  • On a phone Files changed may be hidden to the right of the tabs. Swipe sideways.

steps.title: Releases and GitHub Pages
steps.html:
Look at Releases on the right of the repository page (below, on a phone).

ReleaseThe finished version people download. EarllnCore's Android app (APK) is here
GitHub PagesServes repository files as a free website. You use it in App 2–3 to get your app's address
ActionsA robot that does set jobs automatically. For EarllnCore, Actions builds the APK on every merge

steps.title: Safety quiz
steps.html: While building an app, you got an API key (a password-like string for using a service) to add a map. Can you paste that key into index.html in a Public repository?

steps.title: Oops, think again
steps.html: Anyone can see every file in a Public repository, including past commits. Others could use your key in your name, and you could be billed. Deleting it later doesn't remove it from the history.

steps.title: Right! Three rules to keep
steps.html:
1. Keep passwords, API keys and personal data out of repositories. (If you upload one by mistake, deleting isn't enough: replace the key.)
  2. Notes and work files go Private; only apps for everyone go Public.
  3. Install the Claude app on selected repositories only.

steps.title: 🎉 GitHub at a glance: done!
steps.html:
RepositoryOne folder in GitHub (Public · Private)
CommitOne saved record
BranchA side copy that leaves the original (main) alone
PRA review request to merge changes into the original
MergeReview and combine into the original = final permission
ReleaseThe finished version to download
PagesA repository as a free website
